summary.headline: IMFA's Q2 FY27 earnings rose sharply on new capacity and better prices; FY27 production guidance trimmed to 380,000 tons.
summary.overview: Management said Q2 and H1 FY27 were noticeably higher year on year, driven by new capacity (KNR-2 acquired from Tata Steel, started March 2026) and better prices than last year. KNR-2 reached about 84,000 tpa run-rate in October and is expected to hit 100,000 tpa once transformers are replaced by December. Ferrochrome prices moderated from Q1 to Q2 (average about INR1.165 lakh/ton in Q2) and are expected to ease slightly further in Q3, while metallurgical coke costs are rising. Management guided FY27 production to 380,000 tons (cut from earlier plans due to lower KNR-1 output and a slight KNR-2 delay) and FY28 to about 475,000 tons. The board approved about INR375 crore of capex for Mahagiri underground ore expansion (6 to 7.5 lakh tpa) and low-carbon ferrochrome.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin was close to 30%; margin has moderated since

financial_highlights.value: 161,255 tons (as cited by analyst; not restated by management)

financial_highlights.change: up from INR85,884/ton per analyst citing the presentation

financial_highlights.metric: Notional forex MTM loss in other expenses
financial_highlights.change: USD/INR 95.98 at Sept-end vs 94.6 at June-end

segments.name: Kalinganagar (KNR-1, greenfield)
segments.commentary: First furnace achieved hot metal tapping on 25 August 2026; second furnace tapping expected around 15 November 2026. Management expects output above 100,000 tons in Q3 FY27 for the first time.

segments.name: Kalinganagar (KNR-2, acquired from Tata Steel)
segments.commentary: Operations began March 2026; reached about 84,000 tpa rated run-rate in October, with full 100,000 tpa from four furnaces expected by December after transformer changes in two furnaces. Seventh furnace (partially built at KNR-2) targeted around July 2027.

segments.name: Choudwar and Therubali
segments.commentary: Choudwar produces about 150,000-160,000 tons with lower cost; Therubali (about 100,000 tons) is INR6,000-6,500/ton more expensive. Therubali to be scaled back eventually, not in the next one to two years.

segments.name: Chrome ore mining (Sukinda, Mahagiri)
segments.commentary: FY27 ore raising target 1 million tons; short-term target 1.2 million tons (0.6 Sukinda, 0.6 Mahagiri underground). Q2 ore raising was lower due to extended monsoon hitting open-cast output. Board approved capex to lift Mahagiri to 0.75 million tpa in 50,000 tpa increments starting 2029.

segments.name: Niche / low-phos and low-carbon ferrochrome
segments.commentary: Niche low-phos grade output about 10,000-12,000 tpa (0.015% P max, 15-20% premium); about 70% placed under a long-term 2027 contract with a Japanese customer. Low-carbon ferrochrome targeted by early 2028 at about 20,000 tpa.

segments.name: Ethanol project (120 KLD)
segments.commentary: Expected commissioning January 2027 per analyst; management projects annual revenue about INR320 crore, EBITDA about 10%, internal IRR 15%, ROCE 13-15%, working capital 45-60 days.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production volume guidance kept at 380,000 tons; Q3 FY27 expected above 100,000 tons and Q4 higher to reach 380,000 tons; sales expected to broadly match production.
FY28 volume guidance about 475,000 tons; by 2028 target sales split about 60:40 export:domestic (about 300,000 tons export, 200,000 tons domestic).
EBITDA per ton expected to be INR1,500-2,000 higher over a 12-18 month period once Kalinganagar scales up (all else equal). Management declined to give quarterly price or cost guidance.

Renewable power (70 MW first branch from JSW Energy on the GNA-RE corridor) expected by end-November 2026, lowering power costs from Q3 onward. Startup inefficiencies expected to settle by December 2026.
Management expects margins to tighten for a quarter or so, with volume push fully visible from Q3 onward.
capex_capacity: Board approved about INR375 crore capex: Mahagiri underground ore output 0.6 to 0.75 million tpa (phased from 2029), taking total ore output beyond 1.2 million tons.
Board also approved capex for low-carbon ferrochrome (about 20,000 tpa targeted by early 2028, partly diverted from high-carbon output).

Total ferrochrome capacity cited as 5.34 lakh tons by analyst; smelting capacity to exceed 0.5 million tons with seventh furnace commissioning shortly; KNR-2 partially built furnace targeted July 2027 (timeline to be confirmed in a couple of months).
Ethanol 120 KLD project expected to commission January 2027.
demand_pricing: Q2 ferrochrome price averaged about INR1.165 lakh/ton; management expects slight moderation in Q3 as input costs rise.
Metallurgical coke priced around USD375-380/ton (management's figure, as stated); upward momentum expected due to currency and high trade costs.
Export volume to China about 120,000 tpa currently, expected to rise to 180,000-200,000 tpa. Key stainless customers expanding tonnage; one customer's output rose from 1.5 million to 3 million tons.

South Africa ferrochrome output recovering on special power tariffs for two producers; management expects Chinese capacity to decline and sees global balance in chrome units. Management expects some near-term turbulence.
India stainless per capita consumption about 3.5 kg vs China peak above 8 kg. Management says IMFA's ~17-18 million ton industry share concentration risk is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Status of critical mineral auctions and plans beyond 5 lakh tons of smelting capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: No update; IMFA participated in several auctions without success. Smelting goes beyond 5 lakh tons with the seventh furnace; KNR-2 furnace targeted July 2027, and further capacity will follow the Mahagiri capex.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for metallurgical coke and quantified cost increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify sequential increases; coke cited at about 375-380 with upward momentum. Cost drivers were coke, higher underground ore mix, royalty, startup costs and shipping; EBITDA per ton is about INR28,000 in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Will ore raising in Q2 be lower seasonally and can ore support 1.2 million tons?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, Q2 ore raising is seasonally weak due to monsoon hitting open-cast mining; FY27 target 1 million tons, short-term 1.2 million tons; management expects to exceed 1.2 million tons after Mahagiri expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term contracts and domestic sales plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Most sales are against long-term contracts or repeat customers; 2026 exit was 90:10 export-to-domestic at 160,000 tpa; targeting about 60:40 by 2028 (300,000 tons export, 200,000 tons domestic).

qa_highlights.question: Quantify MTM and stabilisation cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Notional forex MTM loss about INR8 crore in other expenses (USD/INR 95.98 vs 94.6 in June). Startup costs were not quantified; coal price increases and higher volumes raised power and fuel costs.

qa_highlights.question: Ethanol project economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue about INR320 crore, EBITDA about 10%, working capital 45-60 days, internal IRR 15%, ROCE 13-15%.

risks_watch: Q3 and Q4 must deliver about 100,000+ tons per quarter to meet 380,000 tons FY27 guidance; KNR-1 and KNR-2 transformer and furnace ramp-ups are execution risks.
Margin compression from rising metallurgical coke, royalty on higher underground ore mix, shipping costs and startup inefficiencies; EBITDA per ton has already fallen from Q1 levels.
South African capacity restarts could create near-term supply glut before Chinese capacity exits.
Ore raising risk: monsoon seasonality and dependency on underground Sukinda and Mahagiri ramp-ups to reach 1.2 million tons.
Critical mineral auctions unsuccessful so far; no timeline. Renewable power corridor (70 MW) delayed to late November.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and the industry outlook, but cautious on near-term margins: management repeatedly said margins will tighten for a quarter while declining to give numerical cost or price guidance. Answers on critical minerals were brief, and the call was rushed at the end because of time constraints.
key_quotes: we are expecting that due to economies of scale, due to kalinganagar being a more efficient site. We are expecting the margin to be a little bit more robust going ahead.
But even with a marginal moderation of margins going ahead, we have more than sufficient volume to see that in absolute terms, we outperform.
So, our guidance in terms of tonnage continues to be 380,000 tons for FY 27.

growth.why: FY27 production guided at 380,000 t (cut from earlier plans on lower KNR-1 output) and FY28 held at ~475,000 t, backed by KNR-1 furnaces in trial runs, KNR-2 ramping to 84,000 tpa run-rate heading to 100,000 tpa by December, and export volume growth to China; quantified timing exists but revenue growth % was not stated.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: next 2-4 quarters, after a Q3-Q4 tightening
rows.why: Management expects margins to tighten for a quarter or so, with EBITDA per ton around INR28,000 in Q2 versus close to 30% margin in Q1; EBITDA/ton is guided up INR1,500-2,000 over 12-18 months as Kalinganagar scales and renewable power (70 MW) lowers power cost from Q3, offset by rising coke (USD375-380/t) and royalty.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: KNR-1 second furnace tapping ~15 Nov 2026 after first furnace tapped 25 Aug 2026, KNR-2 at ~84,000 tpa run-rate heading to 100,000 tpa by December, with Q3 output expected above 100,000 t for the first time.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 production guided at 380,000 t with Q3 above 100,000 t and Q4 higher; H1 is weak on KNR-1 delays, so H2 must run at roughly 100,000+ t per quarter, and export to China expected to rise from ~120,000 tpa to 180,000-200,000 tpa.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board approved about INR375 crore for Mahagiri underground ore expansion (0.6 to 0.75 million tpa from 2029) and low-carbon ferrochrome (~20,000 tpa by early 2028), so further capex announcements are less likely in the window; seventh furnace capex is already under construction.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 production guidance was cut to 380,000 t from earlier plans, FY28 only held at ~475,000 t, and management is guiding margins to tighten, so an upgrade looks unlikely near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Hitting 380,000 t needs Q3 and Q4 above 100,000 t each after a weak H1, and KNR-1/KNR-2 transformer and furnace ramps, ore raising at 1 million t target (Q2 hit by monsoon) are execution risks.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Low-carbon ferrochrome of ~20,000 tpa targeted by early 2028, and niche low-phos grade (10,000-12,000 tpa, 15-20% premium) already produced with ~70% under a 2027 Japanese contract.

rows.label: Renewable power from JSW Energy (70 MW) lowers power costs
rows.why: 70 MW first branch expected by end-November 2026, lowering power costs from Q3 onward, though the corridor was delayed to late November.

rows.label: China export volume ramp
rows.why: Export volume to China about 120,000 tpa now, expected to rise to 180,000-200,000 tpa as key stainless customers expand tonnage.

rows.label: Ethanol 120 KLD project commissioning
rows.why: Expected commissioning January 2027 with annual revenue ~INR320 crore, EBITDA ~10%, IRR 15%, ROCE 13-15%.
